key_insight: Doc-to-Atom turns a long document into a compact set of reusable "memory atoms" instead of one monolithic adapter. This makes document-conditioned reasoning faster, more memory-efficient, and more flexible across different queries.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the high memory and compute cost of handling long input sequences in LLMs, especially when a single compressed representation must serve many different downstream queries.
method: Compress document context into multiple small "atoms" rather than a single large adapter.
Learn to compile these atoms in one forward pass, amortizing context distillation at inference time.
Compose selected atoms adaptively for different queries, improving flexibility over monolithic document adapters.
impact: For practitioners, this can reduce inference latency and memory usage while preserving document-specific knowledge. It is especially useful for long-document QA, multi-step reasoning, and any setting where the same document must support many queries.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: long document -> atom compiler -> atom bank -> query-specific composition -> answer

paper_title: Doc-to-Atom: Learning to Compile and Compose Memory Atoms
